subject: Model change: Communication lanes, priority signal, and exemption intake
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sam Park <sam@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model change: Communication lanes, priority signal, and exemption intake

Hi team —

We need to lock a clear comms and exemption process for the imminent model variant consolidation scheduled in mid-July. Acme (Sam) flagged potential downstream behavior that requires a short grace period and a formal exemption if they can’t transition by the cutover date.

Asks:
- Product (Irene): confirm last-accept-date for legacy variants and exact tech constraints for a two-week grace flag.
- Sales/AM (Marissa): proposed customer communication cadence and an escalation & approvals flow for exemption requests.
- Ops (Ben): update the comm matrix with routing rules + who owns the fallback model when latency spikes happen.

Attached: initial comm_matrix_v2.xlsx and an exemption_log_template.csv for intake.

Goal: have a published comm lane and a working exemption intake by EOD Friday so Customer Success / AMs can start 1:1 outreach next week.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Product GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model change: Communication lanes, priority signal, and exemption intake

Rishi — thanks for kicking this off. Quick timeline and constraints from product side:

- Last-accept-date (traffic): 2027-07-12T23:59:59Z (after this date legacy variant traffic will be served by bridge with degraded perf but identical logits).
- True rollback is non-trivial; we can keep a two-week grace window by maintaining a compatibility shim but that increases cost and memory by ~12% per host.
- Exemption signal: we can support a "grace" flag at the tenant routing layer for up to 30 days; needs explicit consent in an exemption log entry + AM approval.

Action items for us:
1) I will add a short snippet for the technical requirements to the comm matrix (what the shim affects, perf hit, and how to revert).
2) We need a single approver list (initially: Product Lead + Head of Sales + Ops Lead) — Marissa / Ben, can you confirm?

If we want the grace window without cost surprises for customers, we should offer a credit template or limited burst capacity (Ben, can you estimate capacity delta for a 2-week grace?).

Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Product

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model change: Communication lanes, priority signal, and exemption intake

Looping in a proposed AM/CS cadence for Acme and similar enterprise customers:

- Day 0 (announce): high-level notice with timeline and known behaviour changes + link to FAQ.
- Day 7 (technical deep-dive): invite engineering CS and customer infra for a 45-min session (recorded).
- Day 21 (pre-cutover check): one-off verification call and final opt-in/opt-out decision.

Exemption approvals: I agree with a three-person approver list (Product Lead, Sales Lead, Ops Lead). For speed, we should allow the Sales Lead to approve short (<=14 days) exemptions if Product is looped-in within 24 hours. Anything longer requires Product + Ops signoff.

On credits: offering a one-time migration credit for customers who adopt by Day 21 might be a good lever. If we offer credits, Finance needs to approve a per-tenant cap — I’ll draft a proposal and route it tomorrow.

I will update comm_matrix_v2.xlsx with the AM outreach owners and draft email templates (internal and external).

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model change: Communication lanes, priority signal, and exemption intake

Got it — quick ops numbers:

- Keeping the compatibility shim for two weeks across Acme's dedicated pool: ~1.6x GPU mem usage during peak (estimated). Burst capacity estimate: +40% if traffic stays as-is.
- Cost delta (approx): $2.4k/week for that pool; if multiple tenants request it concurrently we should cap approvals or offer a cost-share.

I updated comm_matrix_v2.xlsx (tab:ops) with routing implications and added a short FAQ entry on performance expectations. I also attached exemption_log_template.csv with a sample entry (tenant id, reason, requested window, AM approver).

Ben
Head of Production Ops

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, PCI Compliance <pci@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Model change: Communication lanes, priority signal, and exemption intake

Sam —

Thanks for the heads-up earlier. Internal alignment is now:

- We will publish a customer-facing timeline next week with the Day 0/7/21 cadence.
- We can offer a short (<=14 day) grace period via a compatibility shim; approvals are available via your AM (Marissa) and count as an exemption entry.
- For longer windows we need Product + Ops signoff; there may be an incremental cost. Ben has added rough cost estimates in the attached ops tab.

Next steps for Acme:
1) Please confirm whether you want the 14-day grace option or need a longer exemption (if longer, please provide target migration blockers).
2) If you choose the 14-day option, Marissa will record the exemption and we’ll apply the shim on your tenant pool the week of July 12.

FYI: I’m attaching the comm_matrix_v2.xlsx and the exemption_log_template.csv. If you prefer, Marissa can set up a technical sync with Irene and Ben for early next week.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Director, Product GTM
Redwood Inference
